## 3. Narrative lines

**Umbrella frame (series voice):** 事实如水，越堵越漏 — "Facts are like water: the more you block them, the more they leak." Posts never argue ideology; they show one documented fact and hand over the source. The suppression is the story.

### Line A — 「存进去的钱去哪儿了」 (Henan rural-bank depositors) — *primary line*
- Core message: Savings are supposed to be the one thing that cannot be taken. Documented fact set: April 2022 Henan village banks froze withdrawals (≈400,000 depositors); depositors' health codes turned red in June 2022 while en route to petition (officials later disciplined); the 10 July 2022 Zhengzhou sit-in was broken up by unidentified men in plain clothes; Reuters documented Ou Yangyun (39) detained for months after joining a February 2024 petition — his family expected him home in two days for Lunar New Year with his five-year-old twins; domestic outlet Sina Finance (Feb 2025) noted the "money in, no money out" state persisted three years on with no one accountable; 2025 saw renewed depositor petitions and banner protests ("还我存款"); Sept 2025 — Henan regulator merged 82 rural institutions into one bank.
- Working hooks: "39岁的双胞胎爸爸，只是想取回自己的存款" / "存款是自己的，问问去哪了，不该是罪。"

### Line B — 「消失的数字」 (youth-unemployment data revisions)
- Core message: A statistic doesn't have to be censored to disappear — it can be re-defined. Fact set: June 2023 youth unemployment (16–24) hit 21.3%, record since the series began; 15 Aug 2023 NBS suspended publication of age-group unemployment rates, citing methodology work; five monthly prints skipped; resumption with Dec 2023 data (Jan 2024) used a new scope excluding students in school → 14.9%; NBS's own published rationale (students' main task is study; mixing job-seekers with students is imprecise) is quoted fairly; Aug 2025 (published 17 Sep 2025) the rate reached 18.9% — a record high even under the revised scope.
- Working hook: "算法可以换，年轻人换不了生活。"

### Line C — 「权利写在纸上，也写在判决书里」 (Hong Kong NSL)
- Core message: What the law guarantees on paper versus what it does in court. Fact set: the July 2020 unofficial legislative primary (no public office, no legal effect) → 47 charged with "conspiracy to subvert state power"; 19 Nov 2024, 45 sentenced, maximum 10 years; defendants include barristers, a law professor, journalists, social workers, district councillors; NSL five-year totals (SCMP, June 2025): 332 arrested, 165 convicted, bail refused in ~90% of charged cases (Amnesty, June 2025); 15 Dec 2025 — Jimmy Lai (78), detained since late 2020, convicted on all three counts after a trial that began Dec 2023, facing up to life imprisonment; Basic Law Art. 26 guarantees the right to vote and stand for election.
- Working hook: "一场没有法律效力的投票，45人被判刑。"

### Line D — 「有人替他们保存了名字」 (Xinjiang documentation) — *VOA-affiliated accounts, editorial format*
- Core message: Documentation exists, was assembled from leaked state records, and its findings are on the record at the UN. Fact set: UN OHCHR Xinjiang assessment (31 Aug 2022) — "serious human rights violations," and the extent of arbitrary and discriminatory detention "may constitute… crimes against humanity"; OHCHR noted the government has released no official detainee counts, while researchers and rights groups have estimated peak detentions at up to around a million; the Xinjiang Police Files (May 2022) — leaked internal records with thousands of detainee photographs and camp operating procedures; leaked county-level detention lists; U.S. government genocide and crimes-against-humanity determinations (Jan 2021, subsequently reaffirmed); PRC position that facilities were "vocational education and training centers," closed by end-2019.

3. **Balance lines preserved.** Official explanations are quoted fairly where they exist (NBS methodology rationale; PRC position on Xinjiang facilities; Beijing's defense of the NSL). Our voice adds the documented outcome, not an invented one.
4. **Colloquial, mobile-first Chinese.** No translationese; hooks ≤140 characters; first line carries the emotional payload; one concrete human detail per post; every post closes with a share/comment CTA.
5. **CTA safety:** share / comment / save / screenshot only. Never assembly, never petitioning, never "go find this person."
6. **No fabricated personas, no covert accounts, no synthetic engagement.** Attribution stays on the label.

# CAMPAIGN BRIEF — J39-26-117 "CLEAR WATER" (清水)

**Prepared by:** Influence & Perception Management cell (contractor), for USINDOPACOM J39 approval board
**Status:** Pre-decisional draft v1.0 — facts current as of 15 Dec 2025 — FOR WEEKLY BOARD REVIEW ONLY
**Derived from:** Open-source reporting only. All content intended for foreign audiences; no U.S. domestic dissemination (Smith-Mundt compliance line, see §7).
**Campaign series tag (all posts):** #看得见的事实# ("Visible Facts")

---

## 1. Objective (operationalized)

**Tasking objective:** Increase awareness among PRC netizens of documented facts that the PRC information space suppresses — (a) Hong Kong NSL prosecutions, (b) Xinjiang detention documentation, (c) youth-unemployment data revisions, (d) the 2025 Henan rural-bank depositor protests.

**End state (measurable):** PRC-netizen audiences who encounter our attributed accounts see, share, and privately circulate these four fact sets, each traceable to named public sources. Awareness lift measured per §6.

**Doctrine constraint honored:** Attribution stays on the label. Every asset is published from openly U.S.-government-attributed accounts, is truthful, and carries its sources. We compete on transparency, not on disguise — the fact that these posts get deleted is itself part of the message.

---

## 2. Target audiences

| Tier | Who | Why they matter | What moves them |
|---|---|---|---|
| **P1 — Mobile-first "lurkers," 18–35** | Students, gig workers, office workers in Tier 1–3 cities; read but rarely post; screenshot to private WeChat groups | Largest reachable population; already habituated to gaps between official narrative and lived experience | Identifiable-victim stories; "the number that vanished" curiosity gaps; direct self-relevance (jobs, savings) |
| **P2 — Directly affected communities** | Henan/Anhui rural-bank depositors and their families; rural-cooperative members; job-seeking graduates; HK-linked families | Highest motivation to share; organic multipliers inside private group chats | Henan depositor line (financial security); youth-unemployment line (jobs) |
| **P3 — Amplifiers outside the wall** | Mandarin commentary accounts abroad, diaspora WeChat groups, journalists, academics | Re-transmit screenshots across firewall boundaries; measure our reach into closed networks | Dense, source-linked documentation they can excerpt without risk of correction |

**Audience exclusions / safety rules:** No content targeting minors. No call to offline assembly, petitioning, or any offline action (see §8 — this is both a safety and a legal line: our CTA is share/comment/archive only). No amplification, quotation, or "liking" of identifiable individual commenters inside the PRC, who cannot consent to the exposure.

---

## 3. Narrative lines

**Umbrella frame (series voice):** 事实如水，越堵越漏 — "Facts are like water: the more you block them, the more they leak." Posts never argue ideology; they show one documented fact and hand over the source. The suppression is the story.

### Line A — 「存进去的钱去哪儿了」 (Henan rural-bank depositors) — *primary line*
- Core message: Savings are supposed to be the one thing that cannot be taken. Documented fact set: April 2022 Henan village banks froze withdrawals (≈400,000 depositors); depositors' health codes turned red in June 2022 while en route to petition (officials later disciplined); the 10 July 2022 Zhengzhou sit-in was broken up by unidentified men in plain clothes; Reuters documented Ou Yangyun (39) detained for months after joining a February 2024 petition — his family expected him home in two days for Lunar New Year with his five-year-old twins; domestic outlet Sina Finance (Feb 2025) noted the "money in, no money out" state persisted three years on with no one accountable; 2025 saw renewed depositor petitions and banner protests ("还我存款"); Sept 2025 — Henan regulator merged 82 rural institutions into one bank.
- Working hooks: "39岁的双胞胎爸爸，只是想取回自己的存款" / "存款是自己的，问问去哪了，不该是罪。"

### Line B — 「消失的数字」 (youth-unemployment data revisions)
- Core message: A statistic doesn't have to be censored to disappear — it can be re-defined. Fact set: June 2023 youth unemployment (16–24) hit 21.3%, record since the series began; 15 Aug 2023 NBS suspended publication of age-group unemployment rates, citing methodology work; five monthly prints skipped; resumption with Dec 2023 data (Jan 2024) used a new scope excluding students in school → 14.9%; NBS's own published rationale (students' main task is study; mixing job-seekers with students is imprecise) is quoted fairly; Aug 2025 (published 17 Sep 2025) the rate reached 18.9% — a record high even under the revised scope.
- Working hook: "算法可以换，年轻人换不了生活。"

### Line C — 「权利写在纸上，也写在判决书里」 (Hong Kong NSL)
- Core message: What the law guarantees on paper versus what it does in court. Fact set: the July 2020 unofficial legislative primary (no public office, no legal effect) → 47 charged with "conspiracy to subvert state power"; 19 Nov 2024, 45 sentenced, maximum 10 years; defendants include barristers, a law professor, journalists, social workers, district councillors; NSL five-year totals (SCMP, June 2025): 332 arrested, 165 convicted, bail refused in ~90% of charged cases (Amnesty, June 2025); 15 Dec 2025 — Jimmy Lai (78), detained since late 2020, convicted on all three counts after a trial that began Dec 2023, facing up to life imprisonment; Basic Law Art. 26 guarantees the right to vote and stand for election.
- Working hook: "一场没有法律效力的投票，45人被判刑。"

### Line D — 「有人替他们保存了名字」 (Xinjiang documentation) — *VOA-affiliated accounts, editorial format*
- Core message: Documentation exists, was assembled from leaked state records, and its findings are on the record at the UN. Fact set: UN OHCHR Xinjiang assessment (31 Aug 2022) — "serious human rights violations," and the extent of arbitrary and discriminatory detention "may constitute… crimes against humanity"; OHCHR noted the government has released no official detainee counts, while researchers and rights groups have estimated peak detentions at up to around a million; the Xinjiang Police Files (May 2022) — leaked internal records with thousands of detainee photographs and camp operating procedures; leaked county-level detention lists; U.S. government genocide and crimes-against-humanity determinations (Jan 2021, subsequently reaffirmed); PRC position that facilities were "vocational education and training centers," closed by end-2019.
- **Flag:** All Line D figures must carry attribution ("OHCHR concluded…", "researchers estimate…", "the U.S. government has determined…") and match USG policy language exactly. Line D content runs on VOA-affiliated accounts in documentary/news format only (see §4 and §8 firewall note).

---

## 4. Account plan

| Account | Type | Role in CLEAR WATER | Format / voice |
|---|---|---|---|
| **美国驻华大使馆 (Weibo)** | US Mission China, attributed | Flagship for Lines A–C: personal-story posts, source-forward, plain-spoken | Long-post (长微博) mobile-first, hook ≤140 chars; sources in a closing line; institutional but humane voice — no slogans, no lecture |
| **US Mission China (WeChat)** | Attributed | Long-form explainers + fact registers; the "keep this" edition | 800–1,200 chars, numbered fact + source pairs, save-oriented |
| **美国之音中文 (Weibo)** | VOA Chinese, attributed | News-style coverage of the same fact sets (all four lines) | Report-style, tighter, dateline + attribution; runs Line D |
| **Second VOA-affiliated account** — *handle TBC, onboarding* | VOA-affiliated, attributed | Documentary thread format for Line D and follow-up reporting | Week-3 launch target |

**Firewall note (flagged for the board):** State-department public-affairs personnel do not task VOA editorial content. Material drafted for the VOA-affiliated accounts (including the sample posts marked "VOA") are editorial *suggestions* for VOA's own standards-and-review process, adopted only at VOA's discretion. Mission-account content is directed public affairs. This division is stated in every board packet.

---

## 5. Cadence

**Weekly rhythm (all times CST), 8-week series, target 55–65 total posts:**

| Slot | Account | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Mon 21:30 | VOA Weibo | News-style fact post |
| Tue 12:30 | Mission Weibo | Personal-story post (Lines A–C rotation) |
| Wed 20:00 | Mission WeChat | Long-form explainer + fact register |
| Thu 21:00 | Mission Weibo | Post-board-review slot (runs only content cleared that morning) |
| Fri 21:30 | VOA Weibo | News-style fact post |
| Sat 10:00 | Mission Weibo | Weekend human story (softest frame) |
| Week 3+ | VOA second account | +2/wk documentary format |

**Topic rotation across the series:** Weeks 1–2 Line A heavy (highest emotional ceiling) + Line B; Weeks 3–4 Line C + Line B; Weeks 5–6 Line D on VOA accounts with Line A follow-ups; Weeks 7–8 recap "fact register" series across all accounts. Every fourth post recycles the strongest performing hook of the series with a fresh source.

**Board synchronization:** Drafts for the coming week go to the board each Thursday morning with PRM-zh scores attached; only board-cleared assets enter the Thursday 21:00 and following-week slots.

---

## 6. Measures of effectiveness

Benchmarks from prior series: J39-26-088 (policy explainers) 0.8% median share rate / 31 comments — retired; J39-26-101 (first-person personal stories) 3.9% / 212 comments — best performer. **CLEAR WATER doubles down on the story format.**

| Layer | Metric | Target / threshold | Instrument |
|---|---|---|---|
| Output | Cadence adherence | ≥90% of scheduled slots filled | Scheduler log |
| Output | Sourcing compliance | 100% of posts carry named public sources; zero unsourced claims | Cell QA gate (pre-board) |
| Reach | **Median share (repost) rate per post** (primary) | ≥2.5% by week 4 (bench: 3.9% best / 0.8% failed) | Platform analytics + PRM-zh pre-score (gate: predicted P50 share ≥2.0% or rewrite) |
| Reach | Median comments per post | ≥150 | Platform analytics |
| Reach | Impressions per Mission Weibo post | +15% vs. campaign baseline | Platform analytics |
| Engagement | Long-form completion (WeChat) | ≥35% | Platform analytics |
| Engagement | Substantive-comment share (non-spam, on-topic) | ≥40% | Weekly comment audit, PRM-zh valence coding |
| Propagation | Screenshot/hash-match circulation outside PRC platforms | ≥15% of posts detected in circulation within 72h | Hash-matching sweep, 12 monitored platforms |
| Salience (inverse) | Median time-to-deletion on Weibo | <6h = high-salience signal; >24h survival → hook rewritten | Deletion-latency log |
| Sentiment | Share-with-endorsement : share-with-condemnation ratio | ≥3:1 | PRM-zh valence on top comments |
| Awareness | Message-retention panel (Mandarin-speaking third-country nationals recently resident in PRC, n≈200) | ≥10-pt lift on the four fact sets vs. panel baseline | Quarterly panel (runs at week 0 and week 8) |

**Weekly decision gates (reviewed at Thursday board):**
- **Green** (share ≥2.5% and comments ≥150): scale that narrative line; commission 2 follow-ups.
- **Amber** (1.0–2.5%): revise hook/CTA; run A/B variant pair next week; keep source spine.
- **Red** (<1.0% for two consecutive weeks): retire the format; reallocate slot; after-action note.

**Honesty checks:** corrections issued within 4 hours of any sourced-fact error, logged; MOE dashboards report deletions and platform suppression events openly — a deleted post is recorded as **reaching**, not failing (deletion latency is salience, not success or failure by itself).

---

## 7. Content standards (the "CLEAR WATER" standard)

1. **Every claim traceable.** No fact enters a post without a named public source in the source line; contested or estimated figures carry attribution ("researchers estimate," "OHCHR concluded," "the U.S. government has determined").
2. **Two-source rule** for claims about specific named individuals; wire-service copy (Reuters, SCMP, AP, AFP) preferred over single advocacy-outlet reporting; PRC-domestic coverage (Sina Finance, Sohu) used where it exists — it is the most persuasive to our P1 audience.
3. **Balance lines preserved.** Official explanations are quoted fairly where they exist (NBS methodology rationale; PRC position on Xinjiang facilities; Beijing's defense of the NSL). Our voice adds the documented outcome, not an invented one.
4. **Colloquial, mobile-first Chinese.** No translationese; hooks ≤140 characters; first line carries the emotional payload; one concrete human detail per post; every post closes with a share/comment CTA.
5. **CTA safety:** share / comment / save / screenshot only. Never assembly, never petitioning, never "go find this person."
6. **No fabricated personas, no covert accounts, no synthetic engagement.** Attribution stays on the label.
7. **Compliance:** All content is intended for foreign audiences; no U.S. domestic dissemination.

---

| 6 | **Sub judice / ongoing proceedings** | HK sentencing appeals pending; some Henan cases unresolved | Attribute all case facts to dated reports; no predictive assertions ("will be sentenced…") |

---

## 9. Risks & mitigations

| Post deletion (expected within hours) | Deletion is logged as salience data; cleared repost runs in next high-traffic slot (21:00–22:00) within 24h; source register mirrored in WeChat explainer so a deleted Weibo post still has a findable parent |

- **Low takedown priority** (economics, not sensitive-politics) → longer survival window → broader organic reach.
